items.title: Can split in legislature party reflect in political party? Supreme Court asks in Shiv Sena symbol case
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday examined whether a split in the legislature wing of a political party could subsequently percolate into its organisation and primary membership. A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana made the observation while hearing the Uddhav Thackeray faction's challenge to the Election Commission of India (EC) decision recognising the Eknath Shinde-led faction as the "real Shiv Sena" and allotting it the bow and arrow symbol. Sibal argued that a split in the legislature party could not by itself amount to a split in the political party. He relied on the Constitution Bench judgment in Subhash Desai v. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday said it will hear a plea flagging disruption of essential services during protests/ strikes. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed that the plea be tagged with another case concerning venues for protests, rallies and gatherings. "When protests are underway, essential services are disrupted. We do not know who is a protester and who is not. Ingress and egress are completely disturbed," the counsel for the petitioner said. "There is already a case pending before us concerning venues for protests, rallies and similar gatherings. Let this petition be tagged with that matter. But tell us, how can we issue a direction of this nature? We will hear the matter," CJI Kant said. A petition is already pending before the top court over the use of Delhi's Jantar Mantar as a site for protests and gatherings. That plea states that Jantar Mantar is no longer a suitable venue for public protests due to safety and logistical concerns. Justice M Nagaprasanna said that criminal investigation cannot be permitted to disable a functioning healthcare institution. items.summary: The Delhi High Court on August 7 expressed shock after being informed that 400 ventilators and 910 oxygen concentrators are lying unused at Guru Teg Bahadur (GTB) Hospital. They are part of a wider list of critical medical equipment lying idle across 26 government hospitals in the city, the Court was told. "The situation of Guru Teg Bahadhur Hospital (GTB Hospital) is also quite shocking where there are 400 ventilators and 910 oxygen concentrators which are lying unused. According to the hospital, the same were required and donated during the COVID-19 pandemic but are now lying in the GTBH Store as they are excess in number," the Court said. The Bench also noted that the hospital's ECG (electrocardiogram) machine is non-functional, with no other ECG machine mentioned in the report, effectively leaving the hospital without one. items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently quashed the appointment of Sadashiva Murthy as a Special Public Prosecutor (SPP) in a case concerning the murder of a Christian priest, on finding that the appointment was made at the request of the complainant (a seminary) [ Father Elias Daniel & Ors v Department of Internal Administration (Police Services ]. Justice Suraj Govindaraj also noted that the SPP's legal fees were being paid by the complainant. In these circumstances, the judge found that the apprehensions of bias raised against such an SPP appointment by the accused were reasonable. "In answering this, this Court casts no doubt at all on the integrity of the Special Public Prosecutor. items.title: President gives assent to law increasing number of Supreme Court judges from 33 to 37
items.summary: President of India Droupadi Murmu has given her assent to the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2026 , which increases the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court from 34 to 38 judges, including the Chief Justice of India. The legislation received presidential assent on August 11 and has been notified in the Gazette of India. The law will be deemed to have come into force on May 16, 2026, when the President had promulgated the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026 . The Act repeals that Ordinance while protecting all actions already taken under it The Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha by Union Minister of State for Law and Justice Arjun Ram Meghwal on July 20. The Lower House passed it on August 3, following which the Rajya Sabha considered and returned it on August 5. It was certified as a money bill under Article 110 of the Constitution. During the discussion in parliament , Meghwal revealed that Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant had written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on May 11 seeking an increase in the Court’s sanctioned strength. items.title: BBC tax raid case: ITAT partly allows appeals, reduces taxable profit in India to 12 percent
items.summary: The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) has partly allowed six appeals filed by BBC Global News Limited arising from the February 2023 Income Tax raids and reduced the profit attributable to its Indian operations from 15 percent to 12 percent of its advertisement revenue [ BBC Global News Limited Vs DCIT ]. A Bench of Judicial Member Vikas Awasthy and Accountant Member Renu Jauhri rejected BBC’s plea to retain the earlier attribution rate of 8.75 per cent. However, it found that the 15 percent rate fixed by the Assessing Officer (AO) was excessive and based on mere estimation. The dispute was over how much of the BBC’s advertising revenue from India could be treated as profit earned through its Indian entity and taxed in India. The BBC argued that the figure should remain at the earlier rate of 8.75 percent, while the Income Tax Department fixed it at 15 percent after finding that the Indian entity performed more functions than the BBC had disclosed. The ITAT agreed that the rate should be increased but found 15 percent excessive and therefore, fixed it at 12 per cent.
